Beyond the rim a marked route sets out across the boggy-in-places plateau to Poor Petes Hut.
The marked route from Poor Petes climbs to a high point of 1115 metres and then gradually descends a broad, undulating ridge, occasionally crossing limestone creek beds.
Maintain the level gradient through the forest on a marked route before merging into clearings where Larrikins Creek Hut sits.

doubts: This page describes two tracks (1000 Acre Plateau; Upper Matiri Valley) plus the Hurricane Hut to Wangapeka Saddle section, each with its own heading, so kind is network. The 1000 Acre Plateau main way has leg times of 3 hr (Lake Matiri Hut to Poor Petes Hut) and 3 hr (Poor Petes Hut to Larrikins Creek Hut), but no whole-way time, so time is null. The Upper Matiri Valley way has leg times of 9 hr and 10+ hr, and no whole-way time, so time is null. The Lake Matiri Hut is the start of both ways (its ref T7 is the hut name). The DOC carpark at Matiri roadend has no road-end feature, so it has no ref. The fork just beyond Bay Creek is not a named place, so its ref is null. Poor Petes Hut, Larrikins Creek Hut and Wangapeka Saddle have no packet entry, so their refs are null. The Haystack side trip is described from The Needle by a ridge traverse, so from is null. Huts include McConchies Hut and Hurricane Hut, which are on the Upper Matiri Valley way rather than the main 1000 Acre Plateau way. The Upper Matiri way's 'unmarked' side-creek route to the tops is not a described way. Exits to Seddonville or Lyell are options for experienced trampers only and are recorded as exits from Larrikins Creek Hut with how 'other' because the page does not say how they are reached.
